title: Annotatio II §.III (1): Irenaeus — Eucharist of earthly and celestial; restricted to use
pass_a_gloss: (1) Two Substances here Irenaeus (A.D. 160), one for all, remembers: The bread, he says, which is from the earth, receiving the invocation of God, is now no longer common bread, but Eucharist consisting of two things, earthly and celestial (Against Heresies bk. 4 ch. 34); but in bk. 5 ch. 12, repeating nearly the same, he adds nonetheless that he wants his words restricted to the use of the sacred Eucharist, in which it comes about that just as celestial souls are nourished by celestial substance as by their proper food, so terrestrial bodies are nourished and grow by terrestrial substance: That Cup, he says, which is a creature, He confirmed as His blood, and that bread which is a creature as His body: When therefore cup and bread receive the word of God, the Eucharist of the blood and body of Christ comes about, from which the substance of our Flesh is increased and consists.
pass_b_english: (1) Irenaeus (A.D. 160) is the stock witness for two things, earthly and celestial, in the Eucharist after invocation.

But bk. 5 restricts the saying to use: celestial souls feed on celestial substance; earthly bodies on earthly — the creature-cup and creature-bread confirmed as His blood and body when they receive God’s word.
source_text: (1) Duas hîc Substantias memorat unus omnium instar Irenæus Anno Dni. 160: Panis, inquit, qui est à terra, percipiens invocationem Dei, jam non communis panis est, sed Eucharistia ex duabus rebus constans, terrena & cælesti, libro 4. contra hæres. cap. 34.; Sed libro 5. cap. 12. idem ferè repetens, adjicit tamen, se verba sua ad usum sacræ Eucharistiæ restricta velle, in quo fiat, ut quemadmodum animæ cælestes, cælesti substantia, ceu alimento sibi proprio, sic corpora terrestria substantia terrestri nutriantur & augescant: Eum, inquit, Calicem, qui est creatura, suum sanguinem, & eum panem, qui est creatura, suum corpus confirmavit: Quando ergo calix & panis percipiunt verbum Dei, fit Eucharistia sanguinis & corporis Christi ex quibus augetur & consistit Carnis nostræ substantia.

lemmas.gloss: of two things, earthly and celestial

notes: Irenaeus two substances; restricted to use.
